claim: toastr's most recent commit is from June 2018 — the project is effectively dead.
quote: updated: 2018-06-16T03:54:40Z — 'Add yarn package manager to the list (#557)'

claim: toastr's latest npm release is 2.1.4 (published Dec 2017) and it depends on jquery >=1.12.0.
react-toastify is actively maintained: v11.1.0 released April 2026, ~13.4k stars.
quote: Latest release v11.1.0 (April 19, 2026); 115 total releases; no deprecation notice.

claim: Sonner is an actively developed opinionated React toast component, latest release 2.0.7 (Aug 2025), ~12.6k stars.
quote: Sonner is an opinionated toast component for React. Latest release v2.0.7, August 2, 2025.

claim: Sonner ~189M npm downloads/month vs react-toastify ~16M and toastr ~132k/week (July 2026).
Sonner's toast API: toast.success/error/loading/promise/custom, id reuse to update a toast in place, action/cancel buttons, description, headless mode.
quote: const toastId = toast('Sonner'); toast.success('Toast has been updated', { id: toastId });

claim: Toaster props: position, expand, richColors, closeButton, theme, dir (ltr/rtl), visibleToasts, offset, toastOptions, icons; multiple toasters via id + toasterId; no progress bar or transition props.
quote: You can render several toasters simultaneously by assigning unique id values and point a toast to a specific toaster via toasterId. dir default: ltr.

claim: react-toastify's ToastContainer exposes hideProgressBar, transition, closeButton, containerId, limit, stacked, rtl, draggable, pauseOnFocusLoss, progressClassName — none of which have direct Sonner equivalents.
quote: autoClose: 5000; transition: Bounce; hideProgressBar: false; containerId: multi-container identifier; limit: max toasts on screen; progressClassName.

claim: react-toastify supports custom enter/exit animations via cssTransition (enter, exit, duration, collapse); Sonner has no transition API.
quote: const Zoom = cssTransition({ enter: 'zoomIn', exit: 'zoomOut', duration: [400, 200] });

claim: react-toastify's toast.update patches render/type/autoClose/toastId on an existing toast; Sonner only replaces content/type by re-calling toast with the same id.
quote: toast.update(toastId, { render: "New content" }); ... when you update a toast, the toast options and the content are inherited but you can update them as well.

claim: Sonner's toast.promise fails against Jest-mocked promises with 'TypeError: n is not a function'; workaround is manual .then/.catch in tests.
quote: When mocking API promises with jest.spyOn, using toast.promise() throws TypeError: n is not a function.

claim: Recommended migration path is a thin wrapper module mapping the old API surface onto Sonner, then swapping the engine behind it.
quote: creating a thin wrapper function that maps react-toastify's API surface to Sonner is a viable intermediate step
